title: Separated Value & Currency Primitives
pattern: Splitting a value and its unit (like currency) into separate primitive fields on a parent entity instead of mapping them as a single cohesive type.
why_bad: An amount has no semantic meaning without its currency. Splitting them enables developers to accidentally perform operations directly on the raw numerical `amount` while ignoring currency boundaries, causing catastrophic conversion bugs.
detection: Numeric fields named `amount`, `balance` directly adjacent to string fields named `currency`, `currency_code` on an entity.
counterexample: Raw data warehouse tables denormalized specifically for high-speed SQL analytics or reporting.
fix:
Group the amount and its currency into a single immutable Value Object.
```rust
struct Money {
    amount: i64,
    currency: Currency,
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (p. 357); *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (p. 488).
